# pulse_inbound_webhook (Resource)

An inbound webhook: an endpoint at `url` that verifies each delivery's signature (GitHub, Stripe, a generic HMAC or a shared secret header) and publishes the request body as an event.

The verification secret is either set with `secret` or generated by Pulse when the webhook is created. Pulse never returns it again, so the provider keeps it in state (sensitive). Change `secret_version` to have Pulse generate a new one. Import with the webhook ID; an imported webhook has no `secret` in state until you set `secret` or change `secret_version`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# GitHub push events for a repository. Pulse generates the secret; paste it and the URL into the
# repository's webhook settings (Content type: application/json).
resource "pulse_inbound_webhook" "github" {
  name = "github-homelab"
  kind = "github"
}

output "github_webhook_url" {
  value = pulse_inbound_webhook.github.url
}

output "github_webhook_secret" {
  value     = pulse_inbound_webhook.github.secret
  sensitive = true
}

# A generic HMAC sender with a timestamped signature, publishing on a custom subject.
resource "pulse_inbound_webhook" "sensor" {
  name    = "sensor-gateway"
  kind    = "hmac"
  subject = "evt.home.sensor.reading"
  secret  = var.sensor_hmac_key

  config = {
    header           = "X-Signature"
    prefix           = "sha256="
    timestamp_header = "X-Timestamp"
    tolerance_sec    = 120
    type             = "home.sensor.reading"
  }
}

variable "sensor_hmac_key" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `kind` (String) How deliveries are verified: `github` (`X-Hub-Signature-256`), `stripe` (`Stripe-Signature`), `hmac` (HMAC-SHA256 of the body in a header, tuned with `config`) or `secret` (the secret itself in a header).
- `name` (String) Name, unique among inbound webhooks: lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`, at most 48 characters, starting with a letter or digit. It is part of `url`, so renaming changes the URL.

### Optional

- `config` (Attributes) Verification and event settings. The header and encoding settings apply to the `hmac` and `secret` kinds only; `github` and `stripe` follow the providers' formats. Unset fields use Pulse's defaults. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config))
- `enabled` (Boolean) Disabled webhooks answer every delivery with 404. Default `true`.
- `secret` (String, Sensitive) Verification secret (at least 16 characters): the GitHub webhook secret, the Stripe endpoint signing secret, or the HMAC key or shared secret. Leave it unset to have Pulse generate one at creation; the generated value is stored in state. Changing a configured value updates it in place.
- `secret_version` (String) Arbitrary value. When `secret` is not set, changing it (including setting it for the first time, e.g. after an import) makes Pulse generate a new secret, which is stored in state. Deliveries signed with the old secret are rejected from then on. Has no effect while `secret` is set.
- `subject` (String) Subject the events are published on (under `evt.`, at least four tokens). Defaults to `evt.hook.<name>.received`, with `_` in the name replaced by `-`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Webhook ID.
- `url` (String) Public URL to configure at the sender (`<public URL>/hooks/<name>`).

<a id="nestedatt--config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config`

Optional:

- `encoding` (String) `hmac`: digest encoding, `hex` (default) or `base64`.
- `header` (String) Header carrying the signature (`hmac`, default `X-Signature`) or the secret (`secret`, default `X-Webhook-Secret`).
- `prefix` (String) `hmac`: text before the digest in the header, e.g. `sha256=`.
- `timestamp_header` (String) `hmac`: header with a Unix timestamp. When set, the signed message is `<timestamp>.<body>` and deliveries outside `tolerance_sec` are rejected.
- `tolerance_sec` (Number) Accepted clock skew in seconds for timestamped signatures (`stripe`, and `hmac` with `timestamp_header`). Default 300.
- `type` (String) Event type (`ce-type`) of the published events. By default `github` uses `github.<X-GitHub-Event>`, `stripe` uses `stripe.<event type>`, and the others `hook.<name>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import with the webhook ID. The secret cannot be read back: set `secret`, or set `secret_version` to have Pulse
# generate a new one.
terraform import pulse_inbound_webhook.github 01jabcdefghjkmnpqrstvwxyz0
```
